bull.b: Royal Caribbean has rebuilt substantial scale and earnings power, with strong margins and net income rising to $4.4B TTM. This profitability supports reinvestment, debt service and resilience across the cruise cycle.

bull.t: Loyalty and digital engagement strengthen demand
bull.b: High app adoption, expanding loyalty enrollment and strong NPS can improve retention, direct engagement and onboard purchasing. These capabilities deepen customer relationships and support durable pricing and ancillary-revenue growth.

bull.t: Debt reduction and refinancing improve capital structure
bull.b: Material deleveraging has reduced balance-sheet risk, while refinancing toward fixed-rate senior notes may lower exposure to rate volatility and extend maturities. Together, these actions improve financial flexibility as operations generate cash.

bear.b: Despite major improvement from 2022, debt remains large relative to equity. A demand slowdown, weaker pricing or higher refinancing costs could therefore pressure cash flow and restrict investment or shareholder returns.

Strong operating cash flow has not recently translated into positive free cash flow after investment and working-capital needs. Continued weak conversion would limit deleveraging capacity and increase reliance on financing for fleet expansion.

bear.t: Mexico destination expansion faces permitting delays
bear.b: The permitting setback creates uncertainty around the timing and returns of a planned destination investment. Delays could defer capacity deployment, reduce the expected contribution from the project and require further stakeholder or environmental work.
